answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can weight every attestation by the structural diversity of its endpoints, not their count. Picture a falcon surveying the trust graph from above: it ignores ivory-tower nodes that only vouch for each other inside tight cliques, because a thousand phantom accounts clustered together add no reach. Each agent's score rises only when endorsements cross separate communities, so manufacturing new identities costs more influence than it buys. Signed claims then work like a cipher: they count as valid only when the key material of diverse peers converges on them.
